newsitem.title: USA: Penn. approves workers' comp rate reduction.
newsitem.headline: Penn. approves workers' comp rate reduction.

text.p: The Pennsylvania insurance department said insurance commissioner Linda Kaiser approved a 25 percent reduction in workers' compensation rates, modifying a filing by the Pennsylvania Compensation Rating Bureau.
The action paves the way for Pennsylvania employers to realize $470 million in workers' comp cost savings, the insurance department said.
The new rates are effective February 1 for new and renewal policies, the department said.
"This monumental reduction in workers' compensation premiums is great news for millions of Pennsylvanians -- both workers and employers," Kaiser said.
"Lower workers' compensation rates help to ensure that Pennsylvania is in the nation's forefront of retaining and creating jobs now and for many years to come."
Kaiser modified the PCRB filing based upon an extensive report submitted November 26 by the independent actuary, Milliman & Robertson, Inc. of Radnor.
The actuary's report projected a 25.4 percent reduction in workers' comp rates.
The rate reduction is the result of workers' compensation reforms signed into law by Gov. Ridge in June 1996 and Act 44 signed into law in 1993, the insurance department said.

Specifically, the reforms, known as Act 57, facilitate the prompt return of injured workers to the workforce; ensure benefits are paid only to legitimate claimants; make certain that benefits are commensurate with pre-injury earnings and reduce the costs associated with litigation and administration of workers' compensation claims.

In addition to the 25 percent rate decrease, employers can, as a result of the new law, achieve an additional 10 percent savings in workers' comp costs through workplace safety committees and strong safety records, the department said.
